_comment: MASTER SYLLABUS TEMPLATE — S5 PRINCIPAL MATHEMATICS

curriculum_metadata.curriculum_name: Advanced Secondary Curriculum Principal Mathematics Syllabus
curriculum_metadata.subject: Principal Mathematics

sub_skills: Predicting outcomes and making reasoned decisions
Working with others to generate ideas
Looking for patterns and making generalisation
Talking confidently and explaining ideas/opinions clearly
Using a range of media to communicate ideas
Using mathematics to justify and support decisions
Using technology to create, manipulate and process information
Using technology to collaborate, communicate and refine work
Respectfully responding to people of all cultures
Appreciating ethnicity as a cradle for creativity and innovation

values: Honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses contextual use of indices, logarithms and surds through mathematical computations for precision, developing analytical skills and making informed decisions to communicate effectively.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: apply the laws of indices and logarithms to solve real life exponentiation problems. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
use properties of surds to solve real-world situations that require precise calculations and accurate results. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through group discussions, learners review powers as indices, laws of indices and simplifying expressions.
In pairs, learners discuss the relationship between logarithms and indices, logarithmic notation and laws of logarithms.
Through group discussions, learners explore how to apply laws of indices and logarithms to solve equations involving indices and logarithms.

By use of internet or other sources, learners demonstrate the applications of the concepts of indices and logarithms in real life scenarios involving exponential growth, decay, or scientific calculations.
In group discussions, learners review rational and irrational numbers, simplify and rationalise surds.
In group discussions, learners solve equations involving surds.
By use of internet or other sources, learners search for and demonstrate the applications of surds in fields such as engineering, art and architecture that require high precision and accuracy.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss indices and relate them to logarithms, noting learners’ ability to; i) interact effectively with others, ii) work effectively in diverse teams. iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.
Converse with learners and judge their ability to convert index notation into logarithmic notation; solve index and logarithmic equations.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness on use of laws of indices and logarithms in solving equations involving exponential growth and decay.

Observe learners as they discuss rational and irrational numbers noting their ability to; i) use numbers and measurements accurately, ii) use mathematics to justify and support decisions iii) show justice and fairness in dealing with others.
Converse with the learners as they simplify and solve equations involving surds and their applications. Evaluate learners’ understanding of the concepts.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness of: i) solutions to equations involving surds. ii) calculations on applications of surds.

topics.core_competency: The learner investigates equations and inequalities to acquire mathematical computational and analytical skills applicable in the real world.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: interpret the solutions of quadratic equations in various real life contexts involving optimisation. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)
apply solutions of linear simultaneous equations in three variables to solve real-world problems involving multiple constraints. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)
apply quadratic inequalities to determine feasible solution sets in real-world scenarios. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)
manipulate polynomial equations and expressions for solving problems in various contexts such as engineering, economics, and physics. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In group discussions, learners review different methods of solving quadratic equations using: Factorisation, completing the square and quadratic formula.
In groups, learners discuss how to express roots as a sum and a product using coefficients of a quadratic equation, and formulate quadratic equations using new roots.
Through think- pair and share, learners solve simultaneous equations that have; linear and non - linear terms, logarithms and equations reducing to quadratics.

Through think- pair and share, learners apply the method of completing squares to: i) determine maximum and minimum values, e.g. maximum profits, minimum costs ii) represent the information graphically, iii) verify the nature of roots of quadratic equations using the discriminant.
In group discussions, learners review: linear equations in one variable linear simultaneous equations in two variables using methods such as substitution, elimination and matrix operations.
In groups, learners discuss how to solve linear simultaneous equations in three variables (in areas such as motion, economics) using elimination, substitution, row reduction and Echelon form.
In group discussions, learners review linear inequalities on a number line and graphs of inequalities.
Through think- pair and share, learners solve quadratic inequalities (such as determining profit ranges and resource allocation) using graphical methods and algebraic techniques.
In pairs, learners use the internet and other sources to discuss applications of quadratic inequalities
In group discussions, learners formulate polynomials to identify the degree of a polynomial.

Through think- pair and share, learners: i) perform long division of polynomials, ii) factorise polynomials, iii) solve equations of the form f(x) = 0 where f(x) is a polynomial of degree three and above.
In group discussions, learners deduce the remainder theorem to find the remainder when the divisor is linear or quadratic.
Through think- pair and share, learners determine the remainder when the polynomial is not known.
In groups, learners find the quotient and remainder of a polynomial with repeated roots.
In group discussions, learners deduce the factor theorem.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they solve quadratic equations, noting learners’ ability to; i) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions, ii) evaluate different solutions, iii) exhibit honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times.

In a conversation, evaluate learners’ ability to explain how to solve simultaneous equations that have; linear and non – linear terms, logarithms and equations reducing to quadratics and techniques of solving quadratic equations with emphasis on completing squares, to sketch quadratic curves, determining their maximum and minimum values and verify the nature of roots using the discriminant.
Assess learners’ written work focusing on formulation of quadratic equations using sum and product of roots and correct use of methods of solving quadratic equations.

Observe learners as they discuss linear simultaneous equations in three variables; focusing on the learners’ ability to: i) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, ii) use mathematics to justify and support decisions, iii) demonstrate social harmony.

In a conversation, prompt learners to explain different methods of solving simultaneous equations in two and three unknowns. Evaluate their solutions through probing questions, use feedback sessions to further deepen their understanding of solving equations.

Assess learners’ product in form of written work focusing on correctness of methods of solving linear simultaneous equations in three variables using elimination, substitution, row reduction and Echelon form.

Observe learners as they discuss quadratic inequalities; note learners’ ability to: i) work independently with persistence, ii) take responsibility for own learning. iii) demonstrate hard work and self-reliance.

Converse with the learners to explain graphical methods and algebraic techniques of solving quadratic inequalities. Check whether they are appropriately applying correct methods of solving quadratic inequalities.
Assess learners’ product in form of written work focusing on the level of understanding of algebraic and graphical techniques to solve inequalities and their applications in real life.

Observe learners as they formulate, solve polynomials and determine remainders of polynomials noting whether they are able to; i) use mathematics to justify and support decisions, ii) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.

In the conversation, prompt learners to explain how to solve polynomials , compute the remainder of a polynomial when the divisor is linear or quadratic, when the polynomial is not known, and when the polynomial has repeated roots. Evaluate learners’ understanding of the concepts.

Examine learners’ written solutions for correctness of formulation of polynomials, long division of polynomials, factorisation of polynomials, determination of the remainder and solving of equations of the form f(x) = 0 where f(x) is a polynomial of degree three and above.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses linear relationships to solve geometric problems and interpret spatial relationships in real-life situations.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine basic coordinate geometry concepts for solving problems related to lines, shapes, and their positions in the plane. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
apply concepts of basic coordinate geometry to solve and interpret geometric problems in real-life situations. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In group discussions, learners review: Cartesian equations of lines, gradients of straight lines intercepts, midpoint of a line, distance between two points, and point of intersection of a pair of lines.
Through think- pair and share, learners use the concept of the mid-point to determine subdivisions of a line and locate coordinates of any point on that line.

In groups, learners discuss: i) the angle between a line and the x-axis, relating it to the gradient of the line, ii) the angle between two lines, iii) the relationship between gradients of parallel lines, iv) the relationship between the gradients of perpendicular lines.
In groups, learners brainstorm how to find the shortest distance between a point and a line.
In groups, learners demonstrate a variety of real-world geometric problems and use ICT related aids or other resources to create a visual presentation of their findings.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss how to solve geometrical problems, focusing on learners’ ability to; i) take responsibility for their own learning, ii) work effectively in diverse teams, iii) demonstrate creativity and innovativeness.
Converse with learners as they do peer presentations, prompting them to explain relationships between coordinate geometric components focusing on understanding of concepts.

Assess learners’ written work and check for the correctness of concepts on: i) intercepts, ii) mid-point of a line, iii) sub-divisions of a line, iv) the angle between a line and the x-axis, v) the angle between lines, vi) the distance between two points, vii) the shortest distance between a point and a line, viii) parallel lines and perpendicular lines and ix) intersection of lines.

Observe learners as they discuss how to apply concepts of geometry of lines to solve real-world problems paying attention to learners’ ability to: i) use mathematics to justify and support decisions, ii) use technology to create, manipulate and process information, iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.
Converse with learners and judge their ability to use ICT related aids to demonstrate geometry concepts and their applications in real life.
Assess learners’ written exercises and ICT presentations to check for correctness of geometric concepts.

topics.core_competency: The learner decomposes rational expressions into partial fractions useful in integral calculus and real-world context.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: Decompose proper and improper fractions into partial fractions for further learning. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners discuss how to express the sum of simple fractions as a single fraction.
In group discussions, learners, express: i) proper algebraic fractions as a sum of simple fractions, ii) improper algebraic fractions as a quotient and proper algebraic fraction.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they express algebraic expressions into partial fractions, focusing on learners’ ability to: i) write and present coherently, ii) talk confidently and explain ideas/opinions clearly, iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.

Converse and probe learners to explain clearly the different types of algebraic fractions and how to break down proper and improper fractions into partial fractions. Evaluate learners’ ability to explain the concepts clearly.
Assess learners’ written work, noting correctness as they decompose proper and improper algebraic fractions into partial fractions.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies trigonometric functions, identities, and equations to solve problems in mathematics and real-life application in navigation, construction, aviation and other fields.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the sides and angles of a right-angled triangle to deduce trigonometric ratios and derive trigonometric identities to solve real-world problems. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)
apply trigonometrical concepts to solve problems related to fields such as navigation, construction, aviation. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through guided discovery, learners: i) review trigonometrical ratios from a right-angled triangle, sine, cosine, tangent of an angle of any magnitude using the quadrants of a unit circle and drawing of graphs of trigonometrical functions, ii) use the trigonometric ratios of sine, cosine, and tangent to determine their corresponding reciprocals, iii) determine trigonometric ratios of 30, 45 and 60, iv) use Pythagoras theorem to derive Sin²θ + Cos²θ = 1, and simplify trigonometrical identities; prove identities, solve trigonometrical equations and eliminate parameters from pairs of parametric equations.
Learners in group discussions, develop the compound angle formulae and use it to deduce the formulae for double angles, half angles, other multi-angles corresponding identities.
In group discussions, learners solve trigonometric equations: involving inverse trigonometric ratios and using t–formulas.

In group discussions, learners use the expressions Rcos(θ ± α) or Rsin(θ ± α) to: i) solve trigonometrical equations of the form a cos θ ± b sin θ + c = 0, ii) find the maximum and minimum of trigonometrical functions involving a cos θ ± b sin θ + c = 0 and 1 / (a cos θ ± b sin θ + c)

In groups, learners discuss and find out how to: i) derive the cosine, sine and tangent rules, ii) solve triangles using the rules, iii) derive the formulae for angles of a triangle in terms of the sides, iv) derive the formulae for area of a triangle.
In pairs, learners use the internet or any other sources, to find out and discuss applications of trigonometry in real life.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners in groups as they discuss trigonometric ratios, derive trigonometric identities, and solve trigonometric related problems, noting learners’ ability to; i) work with others to generate ideas, ii) interact effectively with others. iii) show justice and fairness in dealing with others.
Dialogue with learners noting their ability to explain the different approaches used in deriving trigonometric identities and solving trigonometric equations

Assess learners’ written work to check: i) correctness of the graphs drawn, ii) derivations of trigonometric ratios and identities, iii) eliminating parameters from a pair of parametric equations, and iv) solving trigonometrical equations derived from Pythagoras theorem.

Observe learners as they explore various trigonometrical techniques to solve a variety of trigonometrical equations, noting their ability to: i) evaluate different solutions, ii) identify problems and ways forward. iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.

Converse with learners and judge their ability to explain derivation of the angles and triangles trigonometric properties in solving trigonometric equations and applications of trigonometry in real life scenarios.

Assess learners’ written work to determine the accuracy of: i) derivation of the compound angle formulae and identities, ii) solving trigonometric equations, iii) maximum and minimum of trigonometrical functions, iv) cosine, sine and tangent rules, v) angles of a triangle, vi) area of a triangle. vii) applications of trigonometry, viii) and correctness of the calculations made.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses data through collection, presentation, and evaluation of population parameters and sample statistics in order to predict and plan for self and community development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: present statistical data for prediction and further learning. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse data in order to predict phenomena for purposes of decision making and community development. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through group discussions, learners review how to organise data with equal class width and represent it graphically (histogram and ogive) and make presentations.
In groups, learners explore how to present data with un equal class width on the histogram and use it to estimate mode.
Learners use ICT tools like programmable scientific calculators, smart phones to present real life situations.
In groups, learners review through peer teaching how to determine the average, mode, median, range.
In groups, learners discover how to determine the mode of unequal class width, variance, standard deviation, and estimate percentiles, deciles, quartiles using the ogive.
By use of internet or otherwise, learners do research on how statistics is applied in different fields of learning.
Through discovery, learners use ICT tools like programmable scientific calculators, smart phones to analyse data for prediction of real-world situations.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they review how to organise and present statistical data focusing on their ability to: i) sort and analyse information, ii) evaluate different solutions, iii) demonstrate honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Dialogue with learners as they do the activity; ask questions that elicit them to explain how statistical data is organised and presented.
Assess learners’ written work with emphasis on presentation of data while focusing on neatness, scale uniformity and proper use of graphical techniques.

Observe learners as they compute different measures of central tendency, relative position and dispersion. Note how learners: i) exhibit hard work for self-reliance, ii) sort and analyse information, iii) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions.
Dialogue with learners as they determine and estimate measures of central location and dispersion, focusing on learners’ ability to interpret and interrogate data.
Assess learners’ written work for accuracy of the solutions for statistical measures obtained and correctness of graphs focusing on neatness, scale uniformity and proper use of graphical techniques.

topics.core_competency: The learner investigates the relationship between two quantitative variables through graphical representation and evaluation of correlation coefficients for decision making and prediction.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: determine the correlation between two variables using scatter plots and correlation coefficients for prediction and decision making. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
argue on the relationship between two quantitative variables for prediction and informed decision making. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners through experimentation: i) record and tabulate the values of any two variables, ii) plot the data on graph paper, draw the line of best fit and comment on the relationship between the two variables,
In groups, learners discuss how to rank the data and compute Spearman’s and Kendall’s rank correlation coefficients of a set of data and make presentations.
Learners, through discussion, comment on the values obtained from correlation coefficients and scatter graphs and make presentations.
Learners use the internet or other sources to analyse the applications of scatterplots and correlation coefficients.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners while they explore various methods of interpreting coefficients noting learners ‘ability to: i) use mathematics in justifying and supporting decisions, ii) evaluate different solutions, iii) show honesty; uphold the truth and defend the truth at all times.

Converse with learners and assess their ability to critically analyse the plotted points and explain the relationship between the two sets of data as well as how to compute the correlation coefficients between the two given sets of data.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness of the methodology in computation of the rank correlation coefficients and check for uniformity of scale and correct labeling of the axes on graphs.

Observe learners as they discuss the relationship between variables focusing on learners’ ability to: i) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions, ii) identify problems and ways forward, iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.
Converse with learners to comment on correlation coefficients using different approaches focusing on learners’ ability to listen attentively with comprehension and respect to one another.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness of the comments on the relationship between variables.

topics.core_competency: The learner determines the resultant force and analyses the effect of forces on bodies by applying Newton’s laws to solve problems in real world phenomena.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: determine the resultants of parallel and non-parallel forces for lifelong learning. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
evaluate the resultant of forces in polygons for lifelong learning. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
investigate the effects of friction on bodies in limiting equilibrium and in motion on horizontal and inclined surfaces for problem- solving in different fields of engineering. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
apply Newton’s laws of motion to connected bodies to solve problems involving real- world phenomena. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, through discussion, learners review trigonometrical ratios of sine, cosine and tangent, and explore the application of ratios in finding the resultant of two or more forces acting at a point and make presentations.
In groups, learners discuss how to resolve forces in polygons and determine the resultant force.
Through demonstration, learners review friction, equations of motion and Newton’s laws.
In groups learners experiment the application of friction and Newton’s laws to bodies in limiting equilibrium and in motion on horizontal and inclined surfaces and make presentations.
In groups, learners review Newton’s laws and discuss the application of the laws to the pulley systems.
In groups, learners demonstrate how to apply the Newton’s laws to connected bodies on smooth and rough surfaces for horizontal and inclined planes and make presentations.
In groups, learners use internet, library or any other to demonstrate the application of connected particles in real-life phenomena.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they review trigonometrical ratios, focus on learners’ ability to: i) exhibit integrity; moral uprightness and sound character, ii) work with others to generate ideas, iii) use mathematics to justify and support decisions.
Dialogue with learners and prompt them to explain how the components of a force are obtained. Pay attention to the learners’ ability to apply trigonometric ratios to resolve components.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness and accuracy of the resolved components and the resultant force obtained.
Observe learners as they discuss resultant of forces in polygons. Note their ability to: i) work with others to generate ideas, ii) suggest and develop new solutions, iii) demonstrate social harmony.
Dialogue with learners and judge their ability to explain how the components of force are obtained and hence the resultant force.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness of resolved components, the resultant force obtained and the accuracy in the computations.

Observe learners as they review friction, equations of motion and Newton’s laws paying attention to learners’ ability to: i) work with others to generate ideas, ii) try out innovative alternatives, iii) demonstrate creativity and innovativeness.

Dialogue with learners and prompt them to apply the knowledge of friction, equations of motion and Newton’s laws to bodies on horizontal and inclined rough surfaces; focusing on learners’ ability to work independently with persistence.
Assess learners’ work, check for correctness of the force diagrams, the equations obtained and the use of the S.I units.

Observe learners as they review and apply Newton’s laws of motion, paying attention to learners’ ability to: i) work effectively in diverse teams, ii) listen attentively and with comprehension, iii) exhibit hard work for self-reliance.

Dialogue with learners and prompt them to explain how to apply Newton’s laws to connected bodies on smooth and rough surfaces for horizontal and inclined planes and demonstrate their application in real-world situations; focusing on their ability to write and present work coherently and life skills development.
Assess learners’ work and check the correctness of force diagrams, relative accelerations in pulley systems and SI units.

topics.core_competency: The learner evaluates probabilities through applying the probability laws and theorems to predict the occurrence of events in real life.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: determine the chances of occurrence of events in different aspects for prediction and decision making in the real-world situations. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
apply the probability theorems to predict other occurrences and plan for the future. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners, through demonstration, review the terms; probability, an event, sample space and probability range.
In groups, learners discuss how to generate possibility space using the tree diagram, table of outcomes and explore the use permutations and combinations.

In groups, learners through discussion: i) relate set theory to probability theory and design a contingency table, ii) determine the chance of occurrence of different events in different situations and make presentations.
In groups, learners discuss and explore Bayes’ theorem to determine probabilities of occurrence of events.
In groups, learners explore situations that require the application of probability theory in daily life.
Learners use the library, internet or other sources to brainstorm the applications of probability in real world.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they review the terms used in probability, note learners’ ability to: i) use numbers and measurements accurately, ii) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, iii) exhibit respect for humanity and environment.
Converse and probe learners to explain how to generate sample space using different methods and determine probabilities focusing on learners’ ability to explain the possible alternatives.
Assess learners’ written work; check the accuracy and validity of the probabilities obtained, under various methods focusing on learners’ ability to identify the best method of solving a problem.

Observe learners as they discuss and explore Bayes’ theorem. Focus on learners’ ability to: i) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions, ii) evaluate different solutions, iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.
Converse and prompt learners to explain how to use Bayes’ theorem to obtain probabilities and its application in daily life. Evaluate learners’ understanding of the concepts.
Assess learners’ written work and check for the accuracy and validity of the probabilities obtained by Bayes’ theorem.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies differentiation techniques to solve problems in calculus and interpret their significance in real-world contexts.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore rates of change and slopes of curves using differentiation for further learning. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
interpret the significance of differentiation in calculus and solving real-world problems in fields like Physics, Biology, and Environmental Science. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners discuss how the gradient of a curve at a point can be derived from gradient of a chord using small increments.
Learners, through think- pair and share, deduce the gradient of the tangent at a point on the curve.
In groups, learners through discussions, deduce the formula for differentiation of ax^n, n ∈ R
Through guided group discussions, learners differentiate functions and identify the equations of the tangents and normal curves at different points.
In group discussions, learners differentiate: i) product and quotient functions ii) composite function. iii) parametric functions iv) implicit functions
In groups, learners explore second derivatives of functions.
In groups, through guided discovery, learners determine the maximum and minimum values of given functions.
In group discussions, learners investigate the nature of turning points in curve sketching and optimization of resources.
In group discussions, learners use small changes to approximate roots of numbers, errors in measurements, changes in physical quantities, trigonometric functions etc.
In group discussions, learners apply differentiation concepts to velocity, displacement and acceleration.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they explore different techniques of differentiating algebraic functions paying attention to learners’ ability to: i) work independently with persistence, ii) work effectively in diverse teams, iii) demonstrate hard work for self-reliance.

Converse with learners and evaluate their ability to explain the relation of gradient of a curve to gradient of a line, differentiation formula, differentiation of functions and equations of the tangents and normal to curves at a different point.

Assess learners’ written work to determine the correctness of the gradient of the tangent at a point on the curve, equation of tangents and normal to a curve, differentiation formula, and differentiation of functions.

Observe learners in group discussion as they apply differentiation, noting learners’ ability to: i) evaluate different solutions, ii) identify problems and ways forward, iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.

Converse with learners and prompt them to elaborate on using small changes, the nature of turning points, the different applications of differentiation like curve sketching and kinematics in real life. Focus on learners’ ability to explain the concepts.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness of approximations, nature of turning points and the depth of their knowledge in differentiation.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies integration techniques to solve problems involving areas under curves, accumulation of quantities, and other real-world applications.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: relate integration to differentiation to integrate definite, and infinite integrals. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
apply integration concepts in various fields. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners through guided discovery: i) link integration and differentiation as reverse processes through finding functions which when differentiated return to the original function, ii) associate the limit of summation to the integral sign and evaluate a definite integral using the limits.

In groups, through induction, learners apply integration to: i) determine the area under curve bounded by the x- axis and y- axis and deduce that area is a scalar quantity, ii) determine areas enclosed between two functions, iii) determine displacement, velocity and acceleration, iv) determine the volume of a solid of revolution about: • x – axis • y - axis v) calculate the mean value of a function.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they relate differentiation to integration and evaluate integrals. Note their ability to: i) identify problems and ways forward, ii) evaluate different solutions, iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.

In conversation, prompt learners to discover the relationship between differentiation and integration, noting their ability to critically discover why integration generates a family of functions to understand the implication of the constant of integration.
Assess learners’ written work for accuracy of the integrals and computations.

Observe learners in groups as they discuss applications of integration in various fields focusing on the ability to: i) suggest and develop new solutions, ii) work with others to generate ideas, iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.
Converse with learners and examine their understanding of area, volume, displacement, velocity, acceleration and mean value of a function.
Assess the correctness and accuracy of their computations of area, volume, and mean value of a function.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies the permutations and combinations concepts to solve mathematical problems and model real-world situations.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: apply the concepts of permutations to solve problems in Mathematics, everyday life and other fields such as computer algorithm design, scheduling, and cryptography. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse concepts of combinations to solve problems in Mathematics, everyday life and other infields like genetics, optimisation and statistics. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, through experimentation, learners arrange sets of different objects in a row to distinguish between different arrangements.
In group discussions, learners demonstrate how to arrange a number of different objects in turn to derive the relationship between the factorial notation (!) and number of arrangements.
In groups, through guided discussions, learners perform arrangements of a number of different items to discover that the arrangement of r out of the n objects in a row is given by the formula nPr.
Learners explore different forms of permutations involving: i) identical objects, ii) with or without repetition, iii) with restrictions, iv) circular arrangements.

Through group demonstrations, learners: i) select a set of 2 items from 2, 3 or 4 items to form a group, ii) illustrate how a group of r items can be selected from n items to form a combination, iii) develop the formula nCr used for selecting r objects from n objects to form a group, iv) recognise the difference between permutations and combinations scenarios.
In groups, learners discuss combinations with restrictions.

In group discussions, learners apply knowledge of permutations and combinations in various real-world situations like creation of passwords, pin numbers, team selections, planning menus or outfits etc.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe how well learners arrange the objects, paying attention to their ability to: i) look for patterns and make generalisations, ii) use imaginations to explore possibilities, iii) show creativity and innovativeness.
Converse with learners and assess how they come up with the arrangement,; state the number of arrangements, derive the relationships between possible arrangements of r objects from n objects.

Assess learners’ written work to check for the correct arrangements involving: i) identical objects, ii) with or without repetition,. iii) With restrictions, circular arrangements. Note how accurate their calculations are.

Observe how well learners select r objects from n objects, paying attention to how learners: i) use imaginations to explore possibilities, ii) try out innovative alternatives, iii) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness and sound character.
Converse with learners and probe them to explain how they come up with the selections of r objects from n objects for different scenarios while judging their presentations.
Assess learners’ written work to check how they perform selections with or without restrictions of various situations,

topics.core_competency: The learner applies principles and techniques of series and binomial expansions to understand and solve mathematical and scientific problems in the real world.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse Arithmetic Progression principles to solve problems, recognise patterns and their applications in various contexts. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse Geometrical Progression principles to solve problems, recognise patterns and their applications in various contexts. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
apply the logical steps to establish the truth of a mathematical statement in solving real world problems that require inductive reasoning. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)
apply the binomial theorem to solve real-world problems such as stochastic models, etc. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners through discussion: i) review sequences to identify a series, ii) explore how adding a fixed number to previous terms generates an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.), iii) derive the formula for finding the sum of an A.P, iv) derive expressions for the nth - term of an A.P; apply the derivations to solve numerical problems,

Use case studies, internet or other sources to analyse real life financial scenarios such as investment growth and payment schemes. They examine the patterns and demonstrate the applications of A.Ps in real life situations.

In groups, learners through discussion: i) generate series with a constant ratio between successive terms (G.P) from sequences, ii) derive expressions for the nth term and the sums of a (G.P); apply the derivations to solve mathematical problems, iii) analyse convergence of G.P to generate the sum to infinity of a G.P, iv) use summation notation to determine the sum of any series,
Learners using Socratic circle, discuss the applications of G.P to real- world problems such as compound interest, spread of disease, cell division, radioactivity decay,

In groups, learners design different savings or investment plans using information from a guest speaker from business/ financial sector, or internet or other sources. They discuss which plan might be more suitable based on the client’s goals and timeline.

In groups, learners through experimentation: i) demonstrate simple mathematical statements e.g, the sum of two even numbers is even ii) extend the boundaries of the experiment above and prove that the same statement is still true (say sum of two integers is also even). iii) Under teacher’s guidance, learners explore proving that the same statement is true for any set of even numbers using inductive method.
In groups, learners discuss the validity of other mathematical statements using proof by induction.
Use internet or other sources, learners explore the applications of proof by induction in real life.

In group discussions, learners: i) generate Pascal’s triangle to expand the forms (a + b)^n for n = 1,2,3,4. ii) generate coefficients of terms in the expansion to deduce the binomial theorem, iii) expand binomial expressions in ascending and descending order.
In groups, learners apply the binomial theorem to: i) compute a particular term of binomial expansion, ii) compute roots of numerical values, iii) state range of validity of binomial expansion.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they generate, apply A. Ps to solve mathematical problems; note learners’ ability to: i) look for patterns and make generalisations, ii) use imaginations to explore possibilities, iii) exhibit hard work and self-reliance.
Converse and prompt learners to explain how to generate, identify and apply A.Ps. Evaluate learners’ understanding of the concepts.
Assess learners’ written work to establish the correctness of: i) the formulas for sum of an A. P. ii) nth - term of an A.P iii) report on applications of A.P.

Observe learners as they generate, apply G.Ps to solve mathematical problems; note learners’ ability to: i) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, ii) use mathematics to justify and support decisions, iii) exhibit honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Converse and prompt learners to explain how to generate, identify and apply G.Ps. Evaluate learners’ understanding of the concepts.

Assess learners’ written work to establish the correctness of: i) the formulas for sum, ii) nth - term of a G.P, iii) sum to infinity of converging series, iv) expressing series into summation form, v) report on the different savings or investment plans and their suitability.

Observe learners as they evaluate proofs by induction noting their ability to: i) use mathematics to justify and support decisions, ii) interpret and interrogate data, iii) exhibit honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Converse with the learners and prompt them to explain the logical steps involved in establishing the truth of a mathematical statement. Focus on the logical flow of their explanations.
Assess learners’ written work for correct steps and truthiness of the mathematical statements.

Observe learners as they expand the forms (a + b)^n to deduce the binomial expansion, use it to compute particular terms of the expansion and evaluate roots of numerical values, noting learners’ ability to: i) work with others to generate ideas, ii) look for patterns and make generalisations, iii) exhibit hard work for self-reliance.
Converse with learners and examine how they explain derivation of binomial theorem and how it is used to expand rational functions and how it can be applied to solve real-world problems.
Assess the correctness of derivation of binomial theorem and its applications to compute roots and terms of the expansion.

topics.core_competency: The learner models and analyses the outcomes of random phenomena through determining probabilities and expected values for prediction of uncertainties in real life.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: design different sample spaces and corresponding probabilities of random events to support conclusions and decisions. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse the concept of a probability mass function of a discrete random variable to solve applied problems. ( k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse the concepts of a probability density function of a continuous random variable to solve applied problems. ( k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs through demonstration, learners perform different experiments with coins, pair of die and record the outcomes.
In pairs, learners discuss how to compute and tabulate probability distribution corresponding to a given random event and make presentations.

In groups, learners through discussion: i) describe a discrete random variable and explain the properties of its probability mass function, (p. m. f). ii) determine probabilities, measures of central location and dispersion and sketch the p. m. f of a discrete random variable.

In pairs, learners choose and use appropriate technology effectively in a range of contexts, to produce, plot and investigate the probability of these discrete random variables and their cumulative probabilities.
In groups, learners through discussion, describe a continuous random variable and explain the properties of its probability density function (p.d.f).
Through demonstration, learners determine probabilities, measures of central location and dispersion and sketch the p.d.f and cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variables.
In pairs, learners use technology and other sources to investigate the application of continuous variables in solving problems in real life.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they record and tabulate experimental results, putting emphasis on learners’ ability to: i) write and present information coherently, ii) use a range of media to communicate ideas, iii) exhibit respect for humanity and environment.

Converse and engage learners to explain properties of random variables, probability mass/density function notations and definition of a random variable. Prompt learners to come up with random variables using classroom events; focusing on learners’ ability to ask engaging questions, seek clarification and how they correspond to their findings.

Assess learners’ sample spaces to determine how well the learner can: i) draw sample spaces outcome of tossing coin(s), dice, pair of dice, ii) develop the probability distributions of random events for the sample spaces above, iii) illustrate properties of random variables.

Observe learners as they describe and apply the probability mass functions to solve problems, focusing on their ability to: i) sort and analyse information, ii) identify problems and ways forward, iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.

Converse with learners as they analyse discrete random variables. Assess their ability to describe the concept of a discrete random variable, its probability distribution, and how to compute parameters and draw graphs. Guide learners to construct arguments to prove and justify results.

Assess learners’ written work for coherence, accuracy of the calculations and proper graphical techniques. Determine whether there is evidence that a learner can: i) articulate discrete random variable characteristics, ii) illustrate a probability distribution for a discrete random variable and its properties, iii) compute probabilities corresponding to a given random variable, iv) calculate the mean and the variance of a discrete random variable, v) interpret the mean and the variance of a discrete random variable, vi) solve problems involving mean and variance of probability distributions, vii) calculate the mode, median, CDF (F(X)) and probability distribution table of a discrete random variable.

Observe learners as they describe and apply the probability density functions of continuous random variables, noting learners’ ability to: i) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, ii) write and present coherently, iii) exhibit hard work for self-reliance.

Converse with learners as they analyse continuous random variables. Prompt them to determine probabilities, measures of central location and dispersion, sketch the p.d.f and c.d.f of continuous random variables. Focus on learners’ computation and graphical skills.

Assess learners’ written work for coherence, accuracy of the calculations and proper graphical techniques. Determine whether there is evidence that a learner can: i) articulate continuous random variable characteristics, ii) illustrate a density distribution for a continuous random variable and its properties, iii) compute probabilities corresponding to a given random variable, iv) calculate the mean and the variance of a continuous random variable, v) interpret the mean and the variance of a continuous random variable, vi) solve problems involving mean and variance of probability distributions, vii) calculate the mode, median, CDF (F(X)) and probability distribution table of a continuous random variable, viii) distinguish between a discrete and a continuous random variable.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates the ability to analyse and apply binomial, rectangular, and normal distributions to solve real-world problems.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: apply the binomial distribution function to solve relevant probability and statistical problems in real life. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
demonstrate properties of the rectangular distribution, using it to solve relevant probability and statistical problems in real life. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse the normal distribution and its properties through graphical representations to solve relevant probability and statistical problems in real life. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
transform a binomial random variable to a normal using continuity correction. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
apply the binomial, rectangular and normal distributions to predict outcomes of random processes in real life. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners through discussion, review combinations and the probability product rule, use them in scenarios with repeated independent events to discover the binomial distribution formula.

In groups, learners: i) perform a binomial experiment and use it to determine probabilities of success p, and failure q, for n trials, ii) discuss and determine probabilities using binomial formula and the mathematical tables, iii) explore mean, mode and variance of a binomial distribution.
In groups, learners carry out an experiment that generates a rectangular distribution to derive its probability distribution function, p.d.f.
In groups, learners: i) discuss and determine probabilities in rectangular distribution using real life scenarios, ii) explore the mean, mode and variance of the rectangular distribution.
In groups, learners explore and discuss properties of normal distribution and how it can be standardised to a standard normal, using graphical representations.
In groups, learners discuss standardisation of random variables and use of normal distribution tables/calculators to determine probabilities
Learners in groups discuss how to de- standardise the normal variables to determine parameters.

In groups, learners through demonstration, perform an experiment tossing a coin 50 times and determine the probabilities of any number of heads or tails obtained. Or they use appropriate ICT tools to visualise the outcomes and compare with the normal distribution.
In groups, learners discuss conditions for a binomial distribution to be approximated by normal distribution and how to obtain continuous variables (Continuity correction).
Through Think pair- share, learners determine the expectation and variance.

In groups, through storytelling and under the facilitator’s guidance, learners i) select data problems of interest in various fields, discuss them, and use the internet and other resources to model them, ii) generate questions and use their skills to answer, interpret and explain the relevance of their findings using appropriate ICT tools.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they generate scenarios with repeated independent events. Note how learners: i) plan and carry out investigations, ii) sort and analyse information, iii) exhibit respect for humanity and environment.
Converse with learners and assess how they use the binomial formula and tables to determine probabilities.
Assess learners’ written work. Check on the correctness of: i) probabilities while using tables or calculators, ii) values (mode mean variance).

Observe learners as they discuss the properties of the rectangular distribution, and how they use it to obtain probabilities. Focus on their ability to: i) write and present work coherently, ii) work independently with persistence, iii) exhibit hard work and self- reliance.

Dialogue with learners as they interrogate the meanings of the mean, mode and variance and to ascertain that they understand why it is called a rectangular distribution. Examine learners’ ability to explain the concepts.
Assess learners’ written work for coherence and accuracy of their calculations.

Observe learners as they discuss the properties of normal distribution, standardising of variables. Focus on their ability to: i) evaluate different solutions, ii) identify problems and ways forward, iii) demonstrate hard work and self-reliance.

Dialogue with learners as they analyse normal distribution probe them to explain how to standardise, and de- standardise variables in determining probabilities and parameters using tables or calculator. Evaluate learners’ understanding of the concepts.
Assess learners’ written work for correctness of: i) standardised values (z values), ii) values read from tables, iii) probabilities.

Observe learners as they discuss their observations from the experiment and as they transform a binomial random variable to a normal using continuity correction. Note how learners: i) work with others to generate ideas, ii) look for patterns and make generalisation, iii) exhibit social responsibility.
Prompt learners to explain their observations, conditions for normal approximation and to determine probabilities and parameters; focusing on mixed abilities as they freely explain concepts.
Assess learners’ work and check on the correctness of: i) continuity correction of values, ii) Z- values, iii) probabilities

Observe learners as they discuss the motivation of their problems of interest, focusing on learners’ ability to: i) try out innovative alternatives, ii) suggest and develop new solutions, iii) show national consciousness and patriotism.
In conversation, ask questions and assess whether the chosen distributions model the problems at hand and the solutions are meaningful in real-life.
Assess learners’ ICT aided presentations and written work, check for appropriateness of the modelling distributions and interpretation of solutions.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses errors in mathematical operations and functions to understand the role of precision and accuracy in problem-solving.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the propagation of errors in mathematical operations and functions. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
apply the knowledge of error analysis to improve the level of precision and accuracy in contextual problems. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, through experimentation and discussions, learners: i) measure lengths, weights, volumes, thicknesses, temperatures, timings etc. using various measurement tools of varying levels of precision and use the measurements to compute and compare sums, differences, products and ratios of similar measurements but from different tools, ii) describe errors, sources of errors, the terms used in error analysis and note cases where errors may arise in mathematical computations and real life.

In groups, learners through peer-teaching explore how to derive and compute absolute, relative and percentage errors, minimum and maximum values/ limits of accuracy in expressions and make presentations.
Through guided discovery, learners use their knowledge of differentiation to derive the formulae for error propagation in functions.

In groups, learners use the internet or other resources to: i) discuss other sources of errors other than measurement, ii) identify problems and use the knowledge of errors to discuss the implications of various error measurements (absolute, relative, percentage, minimum value, maximum value) on the solution to their chosen problems and give presentation.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss propagation of errors in mathematical operations and functions noting their ability to: i) work hard for self reliance, ii) interact effectively with others, iii) work effectively in diverse teams.

Converse with learners and prompt them to explain how errors arise in measurement, determine errors in different mathematical operations, determine the minimum and maximum values/ limits of accuracy, and how errors propagate in functions, focusing on learners’ ability to adapt and manipulate the knowledge of errors and its relevance in real life.

Assess learners’ written work or ICT aided oral presentations to evaluate the accuracy in describing error terms, types and sources of errors and the appropriate formula for propagation of errors in functions.

Observe learners as they discuss other sources of errors, present the motivation of their choice problem. Pay attention to learners’ ability to: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly, ii) work effectively in diverse teams, iii) exhibit national consciousness and patriotism.

Converse with learners and provoke them to explain why various error measures are used to analyse the potential implications of errors in measurement. Prompt them to discuss where else the knowledge of error analysis can be used other than the problem of their choice. Evaluate their explanations.
Assess learners’ written work or oral presentations for correct application of error analysis and the accuracy of their result interpretations.
